source.title: When Do We Not Need Larger Vision Models?
source.authors: Baifeng Shi; Ziyang Wu; Mao Mao; X. Wang; Trevor Darrell

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices; no material truncation or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how model size and multi-scale input affect held-out image-classification performance and reports training losses, using pretrained vision models and task-specific heads rather than the claim versions’ original setups.
record.gate_note: The ImageNet classification scaling results in Table 5 bear on model-size scaling and held-out performance. Other tasks, MLLM results, reconstruction measures, and robotic manipulation do not directly test the mapped versions’ specified behaviors. Cited findings from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares pretrained vision-model size with multi-scale feature extraction, not widening beyond an established zero-training-error threshold. Its instance-discrimination losses do not test fitting fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization. None of V1–V8 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that multi-scale smaller models often compete with larger pretrained models, while larger models retain advantages on rare or hard examples. Pretraining with S2 surpasses the larger ViT in Table 4 (82.4% versus 81.6%); for DINOv2 it improves accuracy but remains below the larger model (80.4% versus 81.9%).
record.recipe_differences: Pretrained vision backbones are frozen while task heads are trained; the study varies model size or image scales rather than training networks from scratch to fit arbitrary labels or sweeping width around a zero-training-error threshold.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by pretrained model family and task; the paper reports exceptions where model-size scaling performs better, including OpenCLIP classification and ViT Huge results.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 5 compares ImageNet linear-probe accuracy across frozen pretrained backbones and image scales. Multi-scale extraction usually improves base-model accuracy, while model-size comparisons vary by family.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-scale feature extraction can improve downstream accuracy of frozen pretrained vision models and sometimes compete with larger backbones.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 3 reports similar instance-discrimination losses for Base-S2 and Large, both 1.206, versus 1.223 for Base. Classification training losses are also comparable or lower for Base-S2. These are capacity proxies, not random-label fitting or interpolation-threshold measurements.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-scale smaller vision models can match larger models on selected training-loss proxies for capacity.

record.problems: The classification evidence uses pretrained backbones and trained task heads, not networks trained from scratch. Training errors for the classification rows are not provided, so the interpolation threshold and train-test gap cannot be assessed. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these results.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the selected ImageNet classification scaling results in Appendix A, Table 5. Other reported downstream task, MLLM, robot, representation-reconstruction, and training-loss results do not directly measure the claim versions’ specified outcomes.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels, natural-label held-out accuracy using the same architectures and recipes, and chance held-out accuracy with random labels.
Test-error behavior as network width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch, including the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V2 limits_scope verdict. Neither the ViT-H decline nor the OpenCLIP multi-scale decline tests V2. All recorded accuracy values match the supplied Table 5; these are method-performance comparisons outside the supplied claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels are not tested.

The study does not use one-hidden-layer ReLU networks, MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10, or establish the width required for zero training error or sweep width past that threshold. The classification models are pretrained vision backbones with trained linear heads.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks trained from scratch is reported.
No adaptive optimizer comparison is reported.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets is reported.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other measure of the train-test error gap is evaluated.
No removal of memorized examples followed by retraining is reported.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ImageNet classification with the reported pretrained ViT, DINOv2, and OpenCLIP models
reader_labels.reason: Held-out accuracy is not uniformly improved with larger size or multi-scale input: ViT Huge falls below ViT Base and OpenCLIP Large with two scales falls below its single-scale result (R5, R16); zero-training-error threshold behavior is not established.
